co_age_axe.descent_text: The last pitch ends on a wide, loose ledge near the top of the face, the same ledge that Stone Monkey and Three Stoners reach. Walk along the grassy ledge toward Chiefshead, then zigzag down to the talus on the safest line, which is visible from above and has only a couple of short third-class steps. A faster alternative is the east and southeast side (third to fourth class) back to the northeast side, or third-class slopes on the southwest side. A ramp that is hidden from above also leads down, but it is easy to get cliffed out there. Parties with double ropes can also rappel the route from the top anchor of All Two Obvious.
co_age_axe.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Age Axe takes the prow at the left end of the northeast face. Go to the left side of the face and round the prow onto the southeast side, where a slab apron with right-facing flakes on its right marks the start. About 100 feet above it is a large roof-capped corner, and the start is roughly 100 feet right of East Prow.

co_east_prow.descent_text: The route finishes on a descent ledge near the top. Walk southwest (to the left when facing uphill) a long way across an open ledge and meadow, following a few cairns and a faint trail. At some point you must downclimb a little to reach the top of a long ramp that falls to the northeast; it is very easy to cliff out if you turn too early or too late, so take care to find the right place. That ramp is unpleasant in wet or icy conditions. A safer alternative is to continue farther along the grassy ledge and zigzag down to the talus, or to descend third-class slopes on the southwest side.
co_east_prow.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. East Prow follows the south nose of Spearhead, a blunt arete that is slabby at its base. The start is the most prominent clean right-facing dihedral just left of the prow, about 100 feet left of where Age Axe begins.

co_obviously_four_believers.descent_text: The upper pitches finish near the top of the face, and from there you walk off as for the other routes on the wall: third-class slopes on the southwest side, or the fourth-class ramp on the east and southeast side. To bail from lower down, rap anchors sit on a large ledge well left of the line above the fourth pitch, and two ropes are needed to get off from there.
co_obviously_four_believers.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The route starts at the left side of the wall, with a long easy first pitch to a double ledge system. The Eye of Mordor, the elliptical feature in the lower left of the wall, lies up and left of the early pitches and seeps even in dry years.

co_prowess.descent_text: The route finishes with the upper pitches of East Prow and Age Axe, so it ends on the same ledge near the top of the face. From there walk southwest along the open ledge toward the cairns and faint trail, then downclimb to the top of the long northeast-facing ramp; the turn is easy to miss and leads to cliffs if overshot. A safer alternative is to keep going along the grassy ledge and zigzag down to the talus, or to take third-class slopes on the southwest side.
co_prowess.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Prowess leaves the ground as East Prow does, then moves up and left into its own systems before merging with Age Axe at the 3-inch crack and corner above the third belay.

co_stone_monkey.descent_text: After the Stone Monkey pitch and the 5.8 crack above it, the line exits to the ledge near the top of the face. Walk off the east and southeast side at third to fourth class, or take third-class slopes on the southwest side, or rappel the route from the top anchor of All Two Obvious with double ropes. If you took the Age Axe finish, the usual ledge walk-off applies: along the grassy ledge toward Chiefshead and a zigzag down to the talus.
co_stone_monkey.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Stone Monkey is a single hard pitch high on the face. Reach it by climbing the first three pitches of Scimitar to a grassy ledge, or the early pitches of Three Stoners.

co_sykes_sickle.descent_text: The seventh pitch steps right around an overhang onto third-class ground below the summit, and a short scramble reaches the top. From the summit, descend third-class scree on the southwest side, or take the fourth-class ramp on the southeast side. Both are loose and disorienting; trend climber's left and do not be discouraged if the line looks like it may cliff out.
co_sykes_sickle.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Sykes' Sickle starts in the middle of the face at two parallel cracks. The first pitch follows the wide, left-arcing crack at the center of the wall, easy to spot from below.

co_three_stoners.descent_text: The final pitch finishes on either the East Prow or the Age Axe line, so you reach the ledge near the top of the face. Walk off along the open ledge southwest, find the top of the long northeast-facing ramp after a short downclimb (easy to cliff out if you miss it), or go farther along the grassy ledge and zigzag down to the talus with a couple of short third-class sections. Third-class slopes on the southwest side are another option, or the east and southeast side at third to fourth class.
co_three_stoners.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. Three Stoners starts on the low-angle slabs at the far left shoulder of the face, traversing up and right to a finger crack where the first belay sits.

co_spearhead_chiefshead_pagoda_long_s_tr.descent_text: After Longs Peak, leave the Keyhole Route and drop off cross-country down the talus slopes into Glacier Gorge; the Trough is one such line. Then follow the trail back out the way you came in. Water on the ridge is hard to find unless snow or runoff is present, so carry what you need.
co_spearhead_chiefshead_pagoda_long_s_tr.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead on Bear Lake Road and follow the Glacier Gorge trail about 5 miles to Black Lake. Past the lake, an unmarked climbers' trail climbs east to treeline, and the route then crosses meadows south to the foot of Spearhead's northeast face. The traverse starts by climbing Spearhead, with a choice of route from the North Ridge up to harder lines.
